summary: Bitcoin is the first decentralized cryptocurrency, created in 2008 by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto. It operates on a peer-to-peer network using blockchain technology and proof-of-work mining. Over time, it has gained mainstream adoption, experienced regulatory actions, and seen significant price fluctuations, reaching $100,000 in 2024.

claims.text: Bitcoin was invented in 2008 by an unknown person under the pseudonym Satoshi Nakamoto.
claims.evidence_quote: bitcoin was invented in 2008 when an unknown person published a white paper under the pseudonym of Satoshi Nakamoto.

claims.text: The bitcoin network was created on 3 January 2009 when Nakamoto mined the genesis block.
claims.evidence_quote: On 3 January 2009, the bitcoin network was created when Nakamoto mined the starting block of the chain, known as the genesis block.

claims.text: The first known commercial transaction using bitcoin was on 22 May 2010, when Laszlo Hanyecz bought two Papa John's pizzas for 10,000 bitcoins.
claims.evidence_quote: On 22 May 2010, the first known commercial transaction using bitcoin occurred when programmer Laszlo Hanyecz bought two Papa John's pizzas for ₿10,000, in what would later be celebrated as 'Bitcoin Pizza Day'.

claims.text: El Salvador adopted bitcoin as legal tender in September 2021, but a January 2025 reform effectively ended its legal-tender status in practice.
claims.evidence_quote: In September 2021, bitcoin became legal tender currency in El Salvador, alongside the US dollar. ... a January 2025 reform removed obligations for businesses and the government to accept it, so many analysts regard its legal-tender status as effectively ended in practice.

claims.text: Bitcoin's market capitalization reached $1 trillion for the first time in February 2021.
claims.evidence_quote: In February 2021, bitcoin's market capitalization reached $1 trillion for the first time.

claims.text: In December 2024, bitcoin price reached $100,000 for the first time.
claims.evidence_quote: In December 2024, bitcoin price reached $100,000 for the first time, as US president-elect Donald Trump promised to make the US the 'crypto capital of the planet' and to stockpile bitcoin.

claims.text: The first US spot bitcoin ETFs began trading in January 2024.
claims.evidence_quote: In January 2024, the first 11 US spot bitcoin ETFs began trading, offering direct exposure to bitcoin for the first time on American stock exchanges.

claims.text: In March 2025, President Trump signed an executive order to establish a strategic bitcoin reserve.
claims.evidence_quote: In March 2025, President Trump signed an executive order to establish a strategic bitcoin reserve.

claims.text: Bitcoin mining consumes large quantities of electricity, with surveyed miners reporting that 52% of their electricity use came from sustainable energy sources.
claims.evidence_quote: Mining consumes large quantities of electricity, with surveyed miners reporting that 52% of their electricity use came from sustainable energy sources

claims.text: The genesis block embedded the headline 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks'.
claims.evidence_quote: Embedded in this block was the text 'The Times 03/Jan/2009 Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks'

claims.text: Bitcoin's supply is limited to 21 million coins.
As of June 2026, the circulating supply of bitcoin was 20,057,778 BTC.
The block reward as of 2026 is 3.125 bitcoins per block.
Bitcoin is pseudonymous, and its use by criminals has attracted regulatory attention, leading to bans in several countries.
claims.evidence_quote: As bitcoin is pseudonymous, its use by criminals has attracted the attention of regulators, leading to its ban by several countries.

claims.text: In 2013, the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) classified American bitcoin miners who sell their generated bitcoins as money services businesses.
claims.evidence_quote: In March 2013, the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) established regulatory guidelines for 'decentralized virtual currencies' such as bitcoin, classifying American bitcoin miners who sell their generated bitcoins as money services businesses, subject to registration and other legal obligations.
